page: Amazon Web Services i7i.12xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at a base clock of 3.2 GHz. The compute subsystem is paired with 320 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and AMX (tile and int8). Memory capacity is configured at 384.0 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 28 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addressing.

Local physical storage is a central characteristic of this instance type, delivering 11,250 GB of integrated NVMe SSD capacity. There are no discrete GPUs provisioned on this configuration, prioritizing dense local NVMe I/O operations and massive volatile memory bandwidth over accelerator-bound compute. The hardware yields substantial memory transfer rates, recording 240.93 GB/sec large-block uncached read and 123.85 GB/sec write bandwidth, supported by a 4099.27 GB/sec cached small-block read speed.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate competitive general compute and memory capabilities. Geekbench scores reach 2,319 in single-core and 20,704 in multi-core metrics, aligning with top-tier performance percentiles. The PassMark suite indicates solid execution with an overall CPU score of 69,056.45, 55,094.62 in encryption throughput, and 26,527.8 on database operational tests. In-memory data structures perform effectively, evidenced by Redis recording 72.52 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput peaks at 86.13 GB/sec.

From an efficiency standpoint, the i7i.12xlarge balances high-density local NVMe storage and fast DDR5 memory within an x86 server profile. While stress-ng execution reports middle-tier scores (2,137.69 single-core and 52,419.98 multi-core), the presence of local high-capacity storage and hardware-accelerated AMX matrix units provides high utility without requiring dedicated GPU infrastructure. This profile is best suited for high-throughput relational databases, transactional data stores, distributed NoSQL systems, large-scale data ingestion, and CPU-driven batch ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.12xlarge is a storage-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 48 vCPUs (24 physical cores), it incorporates 320 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 and AMX matrix acceleration. The platform delivers 384.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory and 11,250 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, alongside a baseline 28 Gbps network interface. It contains no GPUs. Benchmark metrics reveal notable throughput, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,704, 72.52 million Redis SET operations per second, and 240.93 GB/sec large-block uncached memory read bandwidth. With its dedicated storage-to-RAM ratio, the i7i.12xlarge is configured for I/O-intensive workloads such as distributed databases, real-time analytics engines, transactional key-value stores, and enterprise ETL pipelines.
